title: Fire craft
about: Laying a fire that lights first time, lighting it without matches, and keeping it going.

articles.title: Build a fire that lights first time
articles.intro: Most fires fail because there's no tinder or the wood is too big. Gather everything before you light.
steps: Pick a sheltered spot, clear the ground to soil, ring it with stones if you can.
Tinder: a fist-sized ball of dry grass, birch bark, cotton or wood shavings.
Kindling: two handfuls of dry twigs, matchstick to pencil thick (they snap, not bend).
Fuel: thumb- to wrist-thick dry branches, stacked nearby.
Lay the tinder, lean kindling over it in a cone (teepee) with a gap on the windward side.
Light the tinder through the gap, low down. Blow gently at the base.
Add bigger sticks one at a time once the kindling burns well.
avoid: Never light under overhanging branches or on peat/dry leaves.
Never leave a fire alone; drown and stir it until cold.

articles.title: Light a fire without matches
articles.intro: A ferro rod, a battery, or a lens can all light dry tinder.
steps: Ferro rod: hold the striker still on the rod, close to the tinder, and pull the rod back hard. Sparks fall onto the tinder.
Battery: touch both ends of a 9-volt battery to fine steel wool; it glows and lights tinder.
Lens: on a sunny day, focus sunlight through a magnifier, glasses or a clear water bottle onto dark tinder until it smokes, then blow gently.
Catch the first glow with very fine tinder, then fold it into the bigger tinder bundle and blow.
avoid: Don't strike a ferro rod away from the tinder: the sparks cool before they land.

articles.title: Keep a fire going
articles.intro: A good fire needs air, the right wood, and steady feeding.
steps: Add wood before the flames die down, not after.
Lay sticks across each other with gaps so air can flow.
Dry damp wood beside (not on) the fire before you add it.
For the night: a few thick logs, side by side, burn slowly. Bank embers with ash to keep them till morning.
avoid: Don't smother it with too much wood at once.
